claim: V07 §3.5a (3) *Under a span* (l. 1591–1595) defers to §4.3 *Lattice and costs* ('A tracker crosses the under-deck strip only where §4.3 … admits a part-0 way'), then ends 'a `cleared` span's ground is free, as a `cleared` support's is ((2))'. The base's crossing rule — §4.3 (l. 5743–5747) and the way-and-channel table's lead (l. 2573–2578), whose `cleared` clause this round wrote for supports only — keeps a `vault` span's under-deck strip impassable (and, by (6)'s lead, a reservation) whatever the span's `state`, and lets a way cross the rest only under a span within clear width, clearance and `squareDeg`, never along the strip. A cleared `vault` span keeps its arch vault, `collapsed` (V04 §3.5.4 (d) (2)). So after V06 §3.19.2's decline clears a span at a village, the village tracker may cross a cleared `vault` span's strip over its chamber, and a cleared `open` span's at any angle; the base forbids the first and bounds the second. Two builders build different village networks.
required_change: V07 §3.5a (3) *Under a span*: replace 'a `cleared` span's ground is free, as a `cleared` support's is ((2))' with 'a `cleared` support's ring is open ground ((2); §4.3 *Lattice and costs*), and a span is crossed by this rule whatever its `state`'. (If the program rules instead that a cleared span's strip is open ground at every rung, §4.3 *Lattice and costs* and the way-and-channel table's lead say so, V04 §3.5.4 (d) (3) removes a collapsed arch vault a way comes to cross, and V07 keeps its clause citing §4.3.)

claim: The crossing table's row W9, the hand-off down (l. 2706), names T-V7-48 in C3, C4, C5, C6, C8, C10 and C13, each 'as C2'. T-V7-48 (l. 3683) hands down a CITY fixture only with its raised way standing (C2), with its frame growth (C12) and in a later Regenerate. No clause hands down a raised way with a span fallen, a support cleared or toppled, a `vault` span breached, or the way held, repaired or edited. R6-02 (b) (i) asks each cell to name a test that runs it; V05 did this for W12, V07 not for W9. The outcome is the same as C2's by construction, so this is a test list omitting a case its cell names.
required_change: T-V7-48 adds, after 'carried down and meeting the palisade as a standing raised way does;': 'the carried-down CITY fixture handed down again with, before the hand-off, a span over the planned palisade's band `ruined` and, on further runs, every such span fallen, a support by the band `cleared` and one `ruined`, its `vault` span breached, the raised way locked, repaired by `repairRaised`, and its Arch spacing edited — each an *unchanged meeting* at the hand-off (§2.7's crossing table, row W9), the palisade then meeting it as *beneath* reads that state;'.

claim: §2.7's crossing table gives the hand-off down (row W9) for every raised-way state, and its cells W9·C3 (one span over the band fallen), C4 (every span fallen), C5 (a support in or by the band cleared or toppled), C6 (a `vault` span breached) and C8 (held) each read "as C2 · T-V7-48". T-V7-48 holds the hand-off down only with a standing deck — "the carried-down raised way meeting the palisade as it met its CITY fixture's innermost ring" — and with a frame-grown one (C12); its clause "after a support is `cleared` the band stands whole across its footprint" is tied to no hand-off. So no bar runs the hand-off of a ring whose span over it has fallen, whose support is cleared or whose raised way is locked. Likewise W1's last column reports `W_RAISED_CROSSING` once per crossing of a deck line for every W1 trace, VS3's palisade among them, and the village cell W1·C2 names T-V7-48, whose palisade clauses assert no report. Each outcome is defined (*unchanged meeting*, read as *beneath*), the readings are run at a town (T110-2 (7)) and the hand-off's unchanged fabric by T-V7-51, so nothing built changes: a cell naming a test for a case the test does not hold (R6-11's class), MINOR.
required_change: V07 ## 7, T-V7-48: after "its line bent to cross the declared aqueduct under a span and to pass beyond each ramp's foot, no ramp, stair or foot in it," add "each crossing of the palisade's line with a deck line reported `W_RAISED_CROSSING` once (§2.7's crossing table, W1),"; and after "its deck extended by a frame growth before the hand-off down, carried down and meeting the palisade as a standing raised way does;" add "that CITY fixture also handed down after V06 §3.19.2's decline, scripted, has left one span over its innermost ring `ruined` (a `vault` span in one variant), every span over that ring fallen, or a support in the ring's band `cleared`, and once with the raised way locked — in each the hand-off writing nothing of the raised way or the ring's runs, and the palisade read by §2.7's crossing table, *beneath* (its run at its own top beneath each fallen span, no chamber under the `vault` span, the band whole across the cleared support's footprint);".
